title: DALL·E 2 (unCLIP): Text-to-Image with CLIP Latents
hook: Turn a prompt into a CLIP image embedding first, then diffusion-decode that embedding into a picture. A two-stage path from words to vivid, editable images.
key_points: Generates images in two stages: text to a CLIP image embedding, then embedding to image.
A diffusion decoder turns the CLIP image embedding into a final picture.
Builds on CLIP's shared text–image embedding space, hence the 'unCLIP' name.
Showed strong text-to-image quality and supported edits and variations.
Demonstrated CLIP embeddings as a useful bridge for generation.
content_html: Ramesh and colleagues built a text-to-image system that works in two steps: a prior model turns a text prompt into a CLIP image embedding, and a diffusion decoder turns that embedding into an actual picture. Because it inverts CLIP's image encoder, the approach is nicknamed "unCLIP." It produced vivid, prompt-faithful images and supported editing and variations.
extra_html:
How it works

CLIP provides a shared embedding space where matching text and images land near each other. DALL·E 2 first uses a "prior" to map a text prompt into a plausible CLIP image embedding — a compact vector capturing what the image should depict. A diffusion-based decoder then generates an image conditioned on that embedding. Because the embedding captures content and style, you can produce variations of an image by decoding nearby embeddings, or blend and edit by manipulating them.

Why it matters

DALL·E 2 was a high-profile demonstration that diffusion plus a strong text–image representation could generate detailed, creative images from natural language. It popularized the idea of routing generation through CLIP's semantic space, and its results helped push text-to-image from research curiosity into mainstream awareness.

related.title: CLIP: Learning Visual Models from Language
related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

related.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
related.hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

choices.text: A prior maps text to a CLIP image embedding, then a diffusion decoder makes the image

flashcards.explanation_html: The prior turns a prompt into a CLIP image embedding; a diffusion decoder then turns that embedding into the final picture.

flashcards.back_html: It effectively inverts CLIP's image encoder — generating an image from a CLIP image embedding rather than encoding an image into one.

flashcards.back_html: Because the CLIP embedding captures content and style, decoding nearby embeddings yields variations, and manipulating them allows blending and edits.
